You've noticed the shelves lean together a little after hours, as if to talk.|The bell, the lamps, the drift to the doors. You know the alcove on the fourth floor where the last lamp dies.} {Footnote is doing his rounds, tail up.|Rain is loud on the high windows.|{final_year: You wonder who will hide in your alcove next year.|Somewhere a book closes itself with a snap.}} Stay hidden past closing {You read by a stolen candle until the small hours. The library is a different animal at night, and it lets you be.|The shelves lean together and whisper while you read. You catch one word in three, and none of them are kind about the history section.|You read in your alcove till the candle drowns. Walking back across the bridges at two, you feel like a burglar who stole only sentences.} {A shelf shuffles sideways and nudges you, firmly, toward the door. A prefect on the stair watches you evicted by furniture.|The shelves close the aisle behind you like a mouth and walk you to the exit. The story is round the house by breakfast.|Footnote finds you, sits on your book and yowls until the porter comes. The porter tells everyone. Footnote is unrepentant.} Leave with the crowd {You go to bed at a decent hour, which feels almost illicit.|You leave with everyone else and sleep like a shelved book.|You walk out under the dying lamps and sleep well. The alcove can wait for you.}
